description: Hi there! The OY BAY team from Astana is ready to take on NASA Space Apps 2026!  We’ve chosen the Earth observation challenge and are putting together a brilliant project.
summary:
BREAKPOINT GeoSpatial Engine is a globally scalable Earth observation research system and evidence-based land-investigation platform developed for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge.   
The Problem: Rapidly growing cities frequently expand over drained lake basins, seasonal wetlands, and altered landscapes. Static present-day maps hide decades of ecological history, leading to misallocated construction investments, localized urban heat islands, and foundation risks.   
Our Solution: Addressing all five NASA challenge operations, BREAKPOINT selects physically interpretable NASA, USGS, and ESA variables (Landsat 5–9, GPM, ERA5-Land, NASADEM), visualizes 42-year trajectories (1984–2026), quantifies change via nonparametric Theil–Sen slopes, and tests significance with autocorrelation-adjusted Mann–Kendall and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR. Validated on Astana, Kazakhstan, it exposed statistically significant surface warming in the Taldykol wetland zone (+0.175 °C/year LST, q = 0.00154) contrasting with greening in the Astana Green Belt (NDVI +0.00889/year, q = 0.000000074).   
Global Scalability: Built on global satellite archives and automated regional empirical calibration, BREAKPOINT can be deployed to any city worldwide by swapping local cadastral rules, feeding verified historical evidence into a 14-factor screening model with legal vetoes and EVSI-guided geotechnical prioritization.
details:
What It Does and How It Works BREAKPOINT GeoSpatial Engine is a multi-decadal Earth observation pipeline and interactive decision-support platform designed for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Instead of relying on static present-day maps, BREAKPOINT reconstructs 42-year environmental trajectories (1984–2026) to detect hidden ecological degradation, wetland drainage, urban encroachment, and localized surface warming before costly land-development decisions are made.

Our processing workflow executes five rigorous steps:

  1. Multi-Sensor Data Fusion: Ingests cross-calibrated surface reflectance and thermal bands from NASA/USGS Landsat 5 TM, 7 ETM+, 8 OLI/TIRS, and 9 OLI-2/TIRS-2 (Collection 2 Level-2), alongside NASA GPM IMERG precipitation, NASA JPL NASADEM elevation, NASA VIIRS nighttime lights, ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 MSI, ECMWF ERA5-Land climate reanalysis, and EC JRC Global Surface Water records.
  2. Physical Variable Extraction: Computes annual warm-season medians (May–September) for vegetation vigor (NDVI), built-up intensity (NDBI), water presence (MNDWI), and land surface temperature (LST), harmonized across sensors using Roy et al. (2016) linear transformations and cloud/shadow-masked via QA_PIXEL bitmasks.
  3. Nonparametric Trend & Significance Metrology: Estimates robust rates of change using Theil–Sen median slopes and evaluates statistical significance with autocorrelation-adjusted Mann–Kendall tests (Hamed & Rao, 1998) and Benjamini–Hochberg False Discovery Rate (BH-FDR) correction to eliminate false positives.
  4. Multi-Criteria Screening & Legal Vetoes: Feeds verified satellite trajectories into a 14-factor Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA-14) engine calibrated with regional empirical quantiles and protected-area hard legal vetoes (such as wetland buffers and urban forest belts).
  5. EVSI Geotechnical Prioritization: Ranks candidate parcels by Expected Value of Sample Information (EVSI) to prioritize where physical soil drilling and laboratory testing deliver the highest economic risk reduction.

Key Findings (Astana Case Study, 1984–2026) Comparing two adjacent landscapes in Astana, Kazakhstan, BREAKPOINT uncovered opposing trajectories:

  • Taldykol Wetland Zone: Statistically significant surface warming (+0.175 °C/year LST, q = 0.00154), vegetation decline (NDVI -0.0057/year), and built-up expansion (NDBI +0.0029/year).
  • Astana Green Belt (Afforestation Zone): Statistically significant vegetation recovery (NDVI +0.00889/year, q = 0.000000074) and declining built-up signal (NDBI -0.00178/year, q = 0.00308), while its apparent cooling trend (-0.097 °C/year, q = 0.423) was transparently flagged as statistically non-significant after BH-FDR correction.

Benefits, Impact, and Global Scalability

  • Prevents Irreversible Urban Mistakes: Protects urban wetlands and green infrastructure while preventing developers and municipalities from building on unstable, historically waterlogged soils without proper engineering.
  • Globally Scalable Architecture: Because Landsat, GPM, ERA5-Land, and NASADEM provide global coverage, BREAKPOINT can be deployed to any city or watershed worldwide simply by updating the target bounding box and local zoning/protected-area layers.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used

  • Cloud Earth Observation & Geospatial Processing: Google Earth Engine (GEE) Python API (ee), geemap.
  • Statistical & Scientific Computing: Python 3.11, NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall (Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction), statsmodels (BH-FDR multiple-testing adjustment), and SHA-256 cryptographic artifact verification.
  • Interactive Web Platform & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet.js (interactive geospatial mapping), and Chart.js (multi-decadal time-series analytics and printable site-dossier export).

Creativity and Human-Centered Design Most remote sensing tools stop at raw heatmaps that city planners and investors cannot easily interpret. BREAKPOINT bridges the gap between orbital statistics and real-world engineering by combining an AI Site Copilot (which parses plain-language technical site requirements and enforces environmental vetoes) with EVSI borehole prioritization and an independent blind manual validation protocol (300 expert checks across two reviewers yielding 113 consensus reference points).

Critical Factors Considered

  • Sensor Continuity & Autocorrelation: Accounted for the ETM+ to OLI sensor transition, seasonal snow cover (filtering to May–September), and serial correlation in multi-year climate series.
  • Scientific Honesty & Uncertainty: Explicitly separates statistically confirmed trends from noisy signals, and clearly distinguishes satellite surface screening from direct subsurface geotechnical drilling.
